result.description: API-first B2B customer support platform (threads, customers, Slack/email/chat) built on a GraphQL API.
result.auth_detail: Machine-user API keys (plainApiKey_..., sent as Authorization: Bearer) with fine-grained permissions; OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow via self-serve OAuth apps in Settings → OAuth applications.
result.access_detail: No app review found: OAuth apps and API keys are created self-serve in workspace settings, and per-workspace API keys are not a gate. But Plain has no free tier. It has a 7-day no-card trial, then paid plans (Foundation $45/user/mo, Horizon $99, Frontier custom). The pricing page doesn't say which plan unlocks the API, and Plain marketing says API is on all plans. So a developer or end user needs a paid workspace after the trial. Not clearly free self-serve.
result.api_notes: Single POST GraphQL endpoint at https://core-api.uk.plain.com/graphql/v1 with a downloadable schema. Plain's own UI is built on it, so there are no UI-vs-API gaps. Docs cover the most-used operations. Webhooks are also available.
result.blocker: No permanent free tier: only a 7-day trial, then paid per-user plans. Plan-level API gating is unconfirmed on the pricing page. Test credentials need a trial or paid workspace.

evidence.quote: Create a machine user and an API key, and scope it with fine-grained permissions.
To call the API as a user in your workspace, use an OAuth app.
Go to Settings → OAuth applications and click Add OAuth app.
Start with a 7-day free trial, no credit card required.
Foundation is $45/user/month, Horizon is $99/user/month, and Frontier is custom.
This means that there are no limitations in what can be done via the API vs the UI.
Plain itself is built on this same GraphQL API.
The Plain MCP server at https://mcp.plain.com/mcp lets tools like Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor work
Once connected, your AI client can do almost anything you can do in Plain, across nearly 400 tools.
